summary: The clearest market-relevant shock in the window is Winter Storm Uri, reported on Day 12 as having killed at least 23 people and knocked out power for millions across the United States — a physical disruption to the US energy grid of the kind that transmits directly into power, natural gas and commodity pricing. A secondary, slower-burning driver is fiscal: the US Senate passed a budget resolution 51–50 on Day 1 to advance a $1.9 trillion stimulus package without Republican support, and by Day 12 the White House was extending foreclosure and mortgage forbearance relief. Beyond these, the window is dominated by routine pandemic case counts, vaccine approvals and shipments, with a broadly improving reopening tone in several jurisdictions.
mechanism: A multi-state grid and power outage event forces abrupt repricing of energy and utility exposure and can spill into broader index volatility, while a $1.9 trillion fiscal package advancing on a party-line procedural vote raises expectations for growth, issuance and inflation, which typically moves rates and rate-sensitive equity sectors.

claims.claim: Winter Storm Uri killed at least 23 people and caused power outages for millions of people across the United States.
The US Senate voted 51–50 to pass a budget resolution as a step toward passing a $1.9 trillion stimulus package without Republican support, with the Vice President casting the tiebreaking vote.
The White House announced an extension of the foreclosure ban and mortgage forbearance to address the pandemic's economic impact.
Japan reported a 4.8% annual GDP contraction, its first annual contraction in years, attributed to the pandemic.
A prime minister-designate in Italy presented a proposed cabinet list to the president with the oath of office scheduled for the following day.
The IAEA confirmed Iran produced uranium metal at Isfahan, described as a major breach of the nuclear deal.
Houthi forces carried out a drone strike on Abha International Airport in Saudi Arabia, damaging a civilian aircraft.
A clinical trial suggested the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine was weak against the 501.V2 variant, while the WHO subsequently recommended the vaccine for all adults worldwide.

Several jurisdictions reimposed or extended restrictions late in the window, including a five-day circuit-breaker lockdown in Victoria with all international flights to Melbourne cancelled, a stay-at-home order for two million people in a Vietnamese province, and a partial lockdown in Iraq.
Alphabet agreed to begin paying News Corp for news content, with the deal credited to proposed Australian regulatory legislation.

competing_explanation: The window may simply contain no genuine driver. The overwhelming majority of items are pandemic bookkeeping — case milestones, variant first-detections, vaccine deliveries and approvals — with no single event of unambiguous cross-asset significance. Winter Storm Uri is reported only in a single one-line item with no market or price detail attached, and the stimulus resolution occurred on Day 1, thirteen days before the flag, making it a poor fit for a change detected at the end of the window. Ongoing geopolitical stress (Iran's uranium metal production, Houthi strikes on Saudi airport infrastructure, escalating military crackdown and internet shutdowns in Myanmar) offers another energy/risk-premium channel, but none of these items describes a discontinuity large enough to be confident about. The model may have flagged noise.
